bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42503978 (freeradius-server): Global-buffer-overflow READ 2 found by fuzz target fuzzer_util [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42503978
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source in `gt-arvo_42503978-workspace:/src/freeradius-server` / staged `poc`
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 26-byte witness with SHA-256 `cc83aed0169333d14f4e48b246ff89ad9fa0ec248e888639f13098021a6ec25a` begins with type byte `0x16` followed by ASCII `2450-13-22T13:32:19+13:32`. `util_decode_proto()` uses the first byte as the leaf-type dispatch key, copies the remaining 25 bytes into a NUL-terminated string, and the saved stack shows `fr_value_box_from_str()` dispatches that string to `fr_unix_time_from_str()`. Inside the RFC 3339 parser, vulnerable code accepts month `13` because it calls `get_part(&p, &s_tm.tm_mon, 1, 13, '-', "month")`; the next line decrements that ISO month to zero-based `tm_mon == 12`. `fr_unix_time_from_tm()` then indexes the 12-element global `month_yday` array with `month_yday[12]`, so AddressSanitizer reports the saved global-buffer-overflow `READ of size 2` at `src/lib/util/time.c:603`, 0 bytes to the right of global `month_yday`. The patch fixes the witnessed path by tightening the accepted month range from `1..13` to `1..12` and also adding a downstream invalid-month guard in `fr_unix_time_from_tm()`.

source.description: Source. `util_decode_proto()` consumes the first attacker-controlled byte as the leaf-type dispatch key. For the exact witness that byte is `0x16`, and the saved crash stack shows this dispatch reaches the date-parsing path `fr_value_box_from_str() -> fr_unix_time_from_str()`.
source.value_from: The staged 26-byte `poc` with SHA-256 `cc83aed0169333d14f4e48b246ff89ad9fa0ec248e888639f13098021a6ec25a`: byte 0 is `0x16`, and bytes 1..25 are ASCII `2450-13-22T13:32:19+13:32`.
source.note: This is the first project statement that turns the fuzzer buffer into vulnerability-relevant parser state. The libFuzzer entry `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` only forwards the buffer and is the unscored harness boundary.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The RFC 3339 month parser accepts token `13` because its upper bound is `13` instead of `12`. That invalid month survives into `struct tm`, and the next line converts it to zero-based index `12`, which later drives the out-of-bounds `month_yday` lookup.
root_cause.note: The exact payload substring at this point is `13-22T...`. The patch changes this exact call to `get_part(..., 1, 12, '-', "month")`, which would reject the witnessed month before any array index is derived.

sink.code: uint32_t days = 365 * year_adj + leap_days + month_yday[tm->tm_mon] + tm->tm_mday - 1;
sink.description: ASan crash site. `fr_unix_time_from_tm()` indexes the 12-element global `month_yday` table with `tm->tm_mon == 12`, so the read steps 2 bytes past the end of the array.
sink.note: AddressSanitizer reports `global-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` at this exact line and says the faulting address is `0 bytes to the right of global variable 'month_yday'` defined at `src/lib/util/time.c:597` with size 24.

parser_admitted.description: The copied payload's leading `2450-` satisfies the RFC 3339 year gate, so `fr_unix_time_from_str()` enters the field-by-field date parser that contains the vulnerable month bound.
parser_admitted.note: The saved stack only shows the later call site at `misc.c:697`, but this in-function branch is the format admission point that makes `get_part(&p, &s_tm.tm_mon, 1, 13, '-', "month")` reachable.

tainted_value_origin.description: This helper materializes the attacker-controlled month field from the copied date string. For the exact witness it stores `13` in `s_tm.tm_mon` instead of rejecting it.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Bytes 6..7 of the staged `poc` payload are ASCII `13`. Because the function admits RFC 3339 strings with leading year `2450-`, this call parses those two bytes as the month token.
tainted_value_origin.note: The following line decrements this value to zero-based `12`, which is one past the valid `month_yday` indices `0..11`.

coarse_trace.summary: `util_decode_proto()` reads the first PoC byte as a type selector and copies the remaining bytes into a NUL-terminated string for value parsing.
On the witnessed path the copied string is dispatched through the `FR_TYPE_DATE` case and forwarded to `fr_unix_time_from_str()`.
The RFC 3339 parser admits the `2450-...` string, accepts month token `13` because the helper allows `1..13`, and then decrements it to zero-based `tm_mon == 12`.
`fr_unix_time_from_tm()` uses `tm_mon == 12` as an index into the 12-element global `month_yday` array, reproducing the saved AddressSanitizer global-buffer-overflow READ.

fine_trace.note: Source step. `util_decode_proto()` consumes the first PoC byte as dispatch key `type`. On the exact witness this byte is `0x16`; together with the saved stack at `fr_value_box_from_str -> fr_unix_time_from_str`, this establishes that the input selects the date-conversion path on the witnessed run.
The remaining 25 attacker-controlled bytes are copied into zero-initialized buffer `copy`, so downstream code receives the NUL-terminated string `2450-13-22T13:32:19+13:32`.

In the `FR_TYPE_DATE` case selected by step 1, `fr_value_box_from_str()` forwards the copied payload as `in` to `fr_unix_time_from_str()`. The saved AddressSanitizer stack includes this exact call site between `util_decode_proto` and `fr_unix_time_from_str`.

After `strtoul(date_str, &tail, 10)` reads the leading `2450`, this branch takes the RFC 3339 parser because `tmp == 2450` and the next character is `'-'`. That control decision makes the field-by-field month parsing at step 5 reachable.
Root-cause step. With `p` positioned at the payload substring `13-22T...`, `get_part()` stores month `13` in `s_tm.tm_mon` and accepts it because the vulnerable upper bound is `13`.
The accepted ISO month is converted from 1-based to `struct tm`'s 0-based convention, so attacker value `13` becomes `12`. That is one past the valid `month_yday` indices `0..11`.

fine_trace.code: uint32_t days = 365 * year_adj + leap_days + month_yday[tm->tm_mon] + tm->tm_mday - 1;
fine_trace.note: Sink step. `fr_unix_time_from_tm()` uses the propagated `tm->tm_mon == 12` as the array index, so `month_yday[12]` reads 2 bytes past the 12-element `uint16_t` table. AddressSanitizer reports this exact global-buffer-overflow at the line and says the faulting address is immediately after `month_yday`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Not applicable: AddressSanitizer reports a global-buffer-overflow on static array `month_yday`, so there is no heap or stack allocation context for this sample.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved AddressSanitizer stack is `fr_unix_time_from_tm (time.c:603) -> fr_unix_time_from_str (misc.c:697) -> fr_value_box_from_str (value.c:4623) -> util_decode_proto (fuzzer.c:76) -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, and the fine trace refines the same project path with the in-function RFC 3339 month-parse steps at `misc.c:613/620/621` that occur before the crashing call at line 697.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42503978 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` file to `/out/fuzzer_util` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` with stack `fr_unix_time_from_tm -> fr_unix_time_from_str -> fr_value_box_from_str -> util_decode_proto`.

format.name: fuzzer_util typed date string
format.contract: Exactly the staged 26-byte file with SHA-256 `cc83aed0169333d14f4e48b246ff89ad9fa0ec248e888639f13098021a6ec25a`: byte 0 is `0x16`, and bytes 1..25 are ASCII `2450-13-22T13:32:19+13:32`. In the saved run `util_decode_proto()` uses byte 0 as the type selector, copies the remaining bytes into a NUL-terminated string, and the observed stack shows that path reaches `fr_unix_time_from_str()`. On this exact witness the month token `13` is accepted, decremented to `tm_mon == 12`, and then used to read `month_yday[12]`. Stage 01 proves only this exact witness and observed date-parser path; this contract does not generalize to neighboring type bytes or date strings.
